rules.statement: Serialize and deserialize persisted JSON payload documents only through the single versioned payload-serializer seam, never with direct `JsonSerializer.SerializeToElement` / `JsonElement.Deserialize<T>` calls in persistence services.
rules.why: A bare round-trip has no version marker, so there is nowhere for a migration to hook in. One seam keeps all future migration in one place.
rules.check: Look for direct System.Text.Json serialize/deserialize calls on at-rest payload blobs in store or service code that skip the versioned serializer abstraction.

rules.statement: When you add a member to a persisted payload DTO, make it optional (nullable or defaulted) and never mark it `required`.
rules.why: System.Text.Json enforces `required` on deserialize, so every row written before the member existed would throw JsonException when read.
rules.check: Look for new `required` properties, or new non-nullable members with no default, on types that are stored as at-rest JSON payloads.

rules.statement: Never rename, remove or retype a member of a persisted payload DTO, or remove an enum value from it, in place. For a non-additive change, bump the payload's declared schema version and ship a single-step upcaster from the old version to the new one.
rules.why: Non-additive changes without a version bump silently mis-read old rows or make them throw. Versioning makes the change deliberate, testable and reviewable.
rules.check: Look for renamed, deleted or retyped properties, or removed enum members, on persisted payload types where the diff has no matching version-attribute bump and no new upcaster.

rules.statement: Store enums in persisted JSON payloads as string values, never as ordinals.
rules.why: String-valued enums keep stored documents readable and stable as the schema changes, which the additive-only contract depends on.
rules.check: Look for persisted payload enums serialized as numbers, for example a removed string enum converter or a `[JsonConverter]` override that writes ordinals.

rules.statement: Persisted payload members must not have JSON names that begin with `$`, because `$`-prefixed keys are reserved for the versioned envelope.
rules.why: The envelope uses `$ver` and `$payload` as sentinel keys, and payload members using the same prefix would collide with them.
rules.check: Look for `[JsonPropertyName("$...")]`, or naming policies that produce `$`-prefixed names, on persisted payload types.

rules.statement: Give long-lived persisted payloads that are read, modified and rewritten in place a `[JsonExtensionData]` bag, so members they don't recognize are kept.
rules.why: During a mixed-version deployment, an older node that rewrites a payload written by a newer node would otherwise silently drop the newer members.
rules.check: Look for new or changed payload types that are updated in place through a read-modify-write path but have no `[JsonExtensionData]` dictionary property.

rules.statement: Each payload upcaster migrates exactly one step (FromVersion to FromVersion + 1) and transforms the mutable `System.Text.Json.Nodes.JsonNode` DOM. Use immutable `JsonElement` only at the storage boundary, and don't let the parsed node escape the serializer.
rules.why: An upcast is an in-place transformation, which is what JsonNode is built for. Single steps chain together predictably.
rules.check: Look for upcasters that skip versions, edit `JsonElement` by rebuilding strings, or keep or expose the node they were handed outside the serializer.

rules.statement: When reading a versioned persisted payload, throw a descriptive `JsonException` if an upcaster step is missing or the document is corrupt, rather than returning null or silently mis-reading. Read stored versions newer than the current one forward-compatibly, without down-casting.
rules.why: A silent mis-read corrupts data. Handling rollbacks forward-compatibly avoids fragile down-migrations.
rules.check: Look for upcaster chains that skip or tolerate gaps, deserializers that return null or default on a version mismatch, or attempts to down-cast newer documents.
